detailed_description:
Photorealistic live-action rendering with the same character appearance as the references, placed against the background from <Picture 3>. The clip runs 10 seconds.

[Shot 1] <Subject 1> is centered, seated, and facing the lens, against the colorful backdrop from <Picture 3>. She has a very low attention span and looks bored and restless. Over the 10 seconds she performs exactly three small, unrelated actions in this order, spaced out across the clip: she __100bored__. Each action is brief and understated, with a pause between them where she simply sits blankly. Throughout the clip, during and between her actions, <Subject 1> (S1) lip-syncs to the music, her lips mouthing along in time with the female vocals of <Audio 1>, synchronized to each word and pause. She stays seated and in place for the entire clip. Only her eyes, face, and fingers do anything, while her torso, shoulders, and seat position remain still. Her expression drifts between bored, vacant, and mildly curious, and she never holds eye contact with the lens for long.

nodes.title: H3 Latent Pull-Forward (added) - auto clip 1 reference
Resample stage — what these nodes do
widgets_values:
RESAMPLE STAGE (added)

After Pull-Forward has pasted the clean background, the cells that MOVE are given a short second sampler pass (denoise 0.55, 5 steps) so the character is rebuilt from the cleaned-up latent instead of carrying over drift. Cells that are still are masked out (mask 0) and are not touched by the second pass.

H3 Moving Mask: the stable latent mask (white = still) becomes a 'moving' mask (white = resample). The first 7 latent frames (= the first 22 video frames, the Motion Context overlap) are switched off, so the carried-over frames are never re-noised.
Set Latent Noise Mask: only the white cells are re-noised and denoised. The audio latent gets a flat 0.5 mask.
Blend Latents By Frames: keeps the Pull-Forward latent for the first 22 frames (the carried-over context) and fades to the resampled latent by frame 44.

Resample model: like H3-LongTakeNoCuts, the second pass uses the plain FL2VA model (no Turbo LoRA, no other LoRAs), with 5 steps at denoise 0.55 and a random seed each run. The Turbo LoRA is made for its own 8-step schedule and gives a waxy / burnt look on a partial denoise like this. This loads a second model, so it needs more VRAM.

Background reference (auto): Pull-Forward saves shot 1 as the clip 1 reference (output/h3_pullforward/clip1_reference.npz) and every later shot pastes clip 1's background from it. Nothing to bypass. Shot 1 is NOT saved if too little of the picture is stable, or if motion covers the whole screen at any moment; later shots then use their own first stable frame. The first 7 latent frames (22 video frames) are not looked at by that check.

nodes.title: Moving cells (invert stable, skip first 22 frames)
Audio length (not used - Match Audio is off)
Resample model (plain FL2VA, no Turbo LoRA - as in H3-LongTakeNoCuts)
Debug: where does Pull-Forward paste, and where does it regenerate?
widgets_values:
DEBUG VIEW (added)

One video, three panels side by side:

 LEFT   the final decoded clip (full length, before the context trim)
 MIDDLE  WHITE = cells Pull-Forward pasted (frozen). BLACK = cells it left to the sampler.
 RIGHT  WHITE = cells the resample pass re-noised (moving cells). BLACK = protected from the resample (still cells + the first 22 frames).

How to read it: put a blocky or banded area from the LEFT panel in the same spot in the MIDDLE panel. If it is BLACK there, the sampler regenerated it (not a Pull-Forward failure). If it is WHITE there, something is wrong with the paste.

The first ~17 video frames of every stable stretch are black in the middle panel on purpose (anchors are still being collected).
Panels are nearest-neighbour latent cells, so edges look blocky.
